title: When the value isn't there: IFERROR
summary: Understand the #N/A error from VLOOKUP, and show a clear message instead with IFERROR.
intro:
If `VLOOKUP` cannot find the value, it returns the error `#N/A`, which means the value is not available in the table.

To show a clear message instead of the error, wrap the formula in `IFERROR`: `=IFERROR(VLOOKUP(F3,A2:D5,2,FALSE),"Not found")`.

faq.q: Why does `#N/A` appear when the value seems to be there?
faq.a: Usually because of an extra space or a spelling difference, or because the number is stored as text in one of the cells.
Yes, it returns the fallback value for any error, so first make sure the formula itself is right.

find-an-employee.prompt: This is a small company's internal phone list. In `G2`, write a formula that returns the name of the employee whose ID is in `F2`.

what-is-na.prompt: If we type an ID in `F2` that is not in the table, such as 1009, what does `VLOOKUP` with `FALSE` return?
what-is-na.explain: `#N/A` means the value is not available in the table.
options: The last name in the table

iferror-worked-example.prompt: `IFERROR` returns a fallback value if an error appears. In `G3`, type the formula `=IFERROR(VLOOKUP(F3,A2:D5,2,FALSE),"Not found")`.

iferror-yourself.prompt: In `G2`, write a formula that returns the name for the ID in `F2`, or "Not found" if it is not in the table.

iferror-number.prompt: In `H2`, write a formula that returns the extension for the ID in `F2`, or 0 if it is not there.
iferror-number.hint: The extension is in the fourth column.

why-na.prompt: Why might `VLOOKUP` return `#N/A` when the name seems to be in the table?
options: Because the cell has an extra space or a spelling difference
Because the column number is small
